r3: c4,c7

This is like a diagonal staircase downward-right. Bottom row is r5: c6,c7,c8. Cell directly above right end: r4,c8. So L part = {r5 c6,c7,c8, r4 c8}. Keep in place. Move other cells one right.

r5: c6,c7,c8 kept.

r3 c4,c7 -> c5,c8.
r2 c3,c6 -> c4,c7.
r1 c3,c4,c5 -> c4,c5,c6.
Yes.

Input:

r8: c0,c5
r9: c1,c6
r10: c2,c3,c4,c5,c6

Move others right:
r7 c0-c4 -> c1-c5 (output r7 c1-c5)
r8 c0,c5 -> c1,c6 (output r8 c1,c6)
r9 c1,c6 -> c2,c6 (output r9 c2,c6) because c6 kept.
r10 unchanged c2-c6.
Output matches.

So rule clear.

We need assemble exactly 2 demonstration pairs. We can create arbitrary input grids that satisfy and verifier computes output. We should create diverse examples to teach rule. Need use show_transformed_input to add pair. We need output computed by environment. We don't know output until call. We can call with input grid, environment returns input-output pair. Need ensure no overlapping ambiguity? objects(I,T,T,T) with univalued True, diagonal True, without_bg True. So connected components by color including diagonals. Shapes as outlines. Need each shape has lower-right L. We can design simple shapes.

Since we only need give inputs, environment computes output. Let's design two distinct examples with maybe colors 2,3 etc.

But careful: verifier uses objects(I, T, T, T) -> univalued=True, diagonal=True, without_bg=True. Background mostcolor (0) removed. Each object is connected component of same color diagonally. The rule: for each object, find argmax rightmost object among objects of same color? Wait verifier uses colorfilter(x8, color) where x8 = objects with univalued=False, diagonal=False, without_bg=True? Let's decode:

x0 = mostcolor(I) bg.
x1 = objects(I, T, T, T)  # univalued True, diagonal True, without_bg True -> objects as same-colored diagonal connected components
x2 = rbind(objects, F)
x3 = rbind(x2, F) -> objects(I, ?, F, F)? Let's parse: rbind(objects, F) fixes last arg without_bg=F? objects signature (grid, univalued, diagonal, without_bg). rbind(objects, F) sets without_bg=False? Actually rbind(function, fixed) fixes rightmost argument. objects has 4 args, so rbind(objects, F) returns lambda grid, univalued, diagonal: objects(grid, univalued, diagonal, F). Then x3 = rbind(x2, F) -> fixes diagonal=F? x2 has 3 args? rbind on x2 with F fixes rightmost of x2 which is diagonal. So x3 = lambda grid, univalued: objects(grid, univalued, F, F). Then x4 = rbind(x3, T) -> fixes univalued=T. So x4 = lambda grid: objects(grid, T, F, F). Thus x4 is objects with univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=False. So x8 = compose(x4, x7) where x7 = fork(paint, x6, normalize). x7 takes object? Let's decode.

Actually x5 = lbind(canvas, x0) -> canvas with value bg, so x5(dimensions) = canvas(bg, dimensions). x6 = compose(x5, shape) -> given patch, dimensions=shape(patch), canvas bg. x7 = fork(paint, x6, normalize) -> given patch: paint(canvas_bg(shape(patch)), normalize(patch)). This creates a grid of the object's bounding box with object placed at origin. Then x8 = compose(x4, x7): given object (as patch?), x7 returns a grid, then x4 extracts objects from that grid with univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=False. Hm.

Then x9 = fork(colorfilter, x8, color): colorfilter(objects from x7, color(obj)). It takes an object from x1? Actually x9 used on x1 objects. Let's not overdecode. It likely finds shape's connected components.

For our purposes, simple shapes.
